newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Resolute says Bulong mine to proceed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Resolute says Bulong mine to proceed.

text.p: Resolute Samantha Ltd said on Thursday it would proceed with the first stage of the development of its Bulong nickel mine in Western Australia.
Stage one development would cost A$184 million, chief executive officer Michael Carrick told Reuters.
The total resource of Bulong is estimated at 140 million tonnes of nickel ore grading one percent nickel and 0.1 percent cobalt.
Stage One would involve installation of a processing plant which would take about 18 months to construct, Carrick said, with commissioning scheduled to begin in March 1998.
Resolute Samantha initially planned to process high grade ore to take advantage of anticipated high nickel prices in the early years of production.
"In Phase One, we will produce 9,000 tonnes of LME grade nickel, growing to 22,000 tonnes in the second phase," Carrick said.
A decision on whether to commit to the second phase of the project would be made during the first year of operations.
Carrick said Phase Two would cost an estimated A$250 million to A$300 million.
He said the company was in discussions with potential local and international joint venture partners for Phase Two.

Carrick estimated that cash production costs for the first five years would be about US$1.64 per pound of nickel. This cost would decline to 82 U.S. cents a pound after taking into account credit from cobalt, he said.
The offsetting cost benefits from cobalt production was based on an average cobalt price of US$15 per pound.
Carrick said the decision to proceed with the Bulong mine was based on the company's view that there would be good long term global demand for nickel, providing opportunities for new producers.
